title: Art night fridays: Wearable Art Night: Upcycle + Transform
Raptor Migration at its Best
description:
Join CMBO Director Brett Ewald and CMBO Naturalists for this workshop. Bird the “raptor capital of North America” at the peak of diversity. Bird the “raptor capital of North America” at the peak of diversity, when falcons are zipping along the dunes, accipiters are flap, flap, flapping by, buteos are soaring overhead, and eagles are chasing Ospreys. Early October often produces flights in the thousands and is the peak time for Peregrine Falcons and others. It is a rare moment during October in Cape May when raptors are not in view and this concentration of birds should ensure that we almost always have something to look at. Learn how to tell buteos from accipiters, falcons from eagles, at the very edge of your eyesight or right overhead, and focus on tricky species-pairs, such as the many ways to tell Sharp-shinned from Cooper’s Hawks. We’ll visit areas around Cape May to make the most of your raptor watching on this “in the field” workshop. We’ll also be in a prime location to enjoy other migrants, such as shorebirds, late warblers, early sparrows, and more!  
Because of the inherent dynamic nature of birding, we do not pre-set an exact itinerary but will visit those parts of Cape May County that regularly hold good numbers of birds. Final location decisions will be made by the leader based on local knowledge and conditions at the time. We may walk up to 1.5 miles, over generally level, sometimes muddy or sandy terrain.  
PREREGISTRATION REQUIRED – Ticket sales end 24hrs before start of program 


COST: $100 members, $130 nonmembers. 
Interested in becoming a member? Please click on the following link to learn more or join: Become a Member today! 

IMPORTANT INFORMATION: 


We bird in all weather. Be sure to check the forecast in advance and dress in layers appropriate for prevailing weather conditions. The weather in Cape May can differ considerably from nearby inland areas and may be warmer, colder, or windier so it’s best to be over prepared. We may have to bird in the rain, so please bring your rain gear. 



TRANSPORTATION: Please arrive at the appointed time with a full tank of gas, as transportation to field sites is by private vehicles.  We may walk up to 1.5 miles, over generally level, sometimes muddy or sandy terrain. Some trips involve walks over jetties. 


CANCELLATION: CMBO programs require a minimum number of registrants to run, five days in advance of the start of the tour but are seldom cancelled. If we do cancel, due to lack of participation, severe weather, or unforeseen circumstances, we notify all participants in advance, and all are eligible for a full credit or refund. Participants may cancel without penalty if greater than 30 days in advance. Cancellations 10 to 30 days in advance may be subject to a 25% service charge. No refunds or credits for cancellations less than ten days in advance unless due to health emergencies. 




REGISTER HERE

title: Bank of America Museums on Us Weekend: October 3-4
description:
WHAT: Bank of America, Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank cardholders can receive FREE general admission to cultural attractions across New York City and New Jersey on Saturday and Sunday. 
WHEN: Saturday, October 3rd & Sunday, October 4th (+ the first full weekend of each month) 
WHERE: Learn something new this month with a visit to a participating cultural institution, including:
-Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum, 2 East 91st Street, New York, NY 10128
-The Intrepid Museum, Pier 86 W 46th, New York, NY 10036
-The Jewish Museum, 1109 5th Ave, New York, NY 10128 (Sundays only)

WHY: Bank of America believes the arts have a unique ability to connect people and communities and help local economies thrive. Through Museums on Us, Bank of America provides its cardholders with free access during the first full weekend of every month to artistic and cultural experiences in New Jersey at celebrated institutions ranging from art, children’s and history museums to botanical gardens, and science centers. This is one example of how the bank strengthens the local communities it serves in, creates greater cultural understanding, and expands accessibility to the arts. 
HOW: Use the bank’s location finder tool to search for participating cultural attractions. Please check with our partners directly for current operating hours and admission guidelines. Present your Bank of America, Merrill or Bank of America Private Bank credit or debit card along with a photo ID to gain free general admission to any participating institution during the first full weekend (Saturday and Sunday) of each month. Cardholders only; guests are not eligible for free admission. Program excludes fundraising events, special exhibitions, and ticketed shows. Not to be combined with other offers. title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Saturdays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: LINES TO LOVE: Screen-Free Afternoon with Your Child
location: The Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, loft #2, Montclair, NJ, 07042, United States
description:
Lines to Love:  A Creative Space for You & Your Child.
Led by Leo A. Sante
Remember what it felt like to simply be together with the child you love?

No screens, no rush, no expectations.

Just being side by side, doodling, making up stories, letting your imaginations wander wherever they wanted to go. 
Lines to Love brings you back to that space. 
Using a simple roll of paper and a few drawing materials, you and your child will be guided into a playful world of co-creation. 
Together, you’ll follow lines, add to each other’s doodles, build whimsical stories, and let the drawing become a pathway to imagination. 
Lines to Love is inspired by a cherished ritual between a father, Leo, and his young son, Lucas.  Back when Lucas was little, Leo would just roll out paper and two pens. Together they’d spend hours just doodling, creating, and enjoying the precious time together. Both Leo and Lucas cherish those drawings and those moments to this day. 
This is a free flowing togetherness workshop. It’s a rare chance to share precious, screen-free time. To explore, wonder, laugh, doodle quietly. To create something beautiful side by side. 
No artistic skills necessary. Just bring your open hearts.
All materials will be provided. 
You’ll leave with unforgettable memories and a creation you’ll both cherish all your lives. 

Ticket is for an adult + 1 child. The event is structured for 1:1 time.
Additional members of a family are welcome
Each child should be joined by an adult.
All materials will be provided.
All phones will be off and set aside for the duration of the session.
Space is limited to 15 pairs, so we recommend you reserve early.

title: Exploring Hispanic & Afro-Caribbean Genealogy
description:
About the program

If you are just starting out on your path through family history, this interactive and informative lecture, Introduction to Hispanic Genealogy, is perfect for you. This approach, spearheaded by genealogist Irisneri Alicea Flores, streamlines the research process while shedding light on the cultural and historical background of Puerto Rican and Hispanic descent more generally.

By following a four-step process, participants will be able to organize their existing knowledge, conduct interviews with family members, locate relevant family records, and set specific research objectives for their genealogical study. Using online genealogical platforms and historical documents can overwhelm beginners, but this presentation will help them manage their emotions and avoid repeating mistakes.

Spanish naming customs, historical jargon, and cultural context discovered in records are some of the research approaches that are exclusive to Hispanic and Puerto Rican populations. Participants will gain self-assurance in their genealogical work as the course covers typical research mistakes, ways to improve accuracy, and practical procedures.

About the artist

Irisneri Alicea Flores, a professional genealogist, founded Descubre Tu Historia. Originating from Bayamón, Puerto Rico, she is an authority on Latin American, Caribbean, and Puerto Rican genealogy. She assists people in retracing their family trees by means of DNA testing, oral histories, and archival research; she has been doing this work for over 13 years and has a Certificate in Genealogy Research from Boston University. Irisneri, who is fluent in both English and Spanish, has spoken about Hispanic ancestry at events hosted by museums, libraries, and genealogical groups in the United States. Helping people find, keep, and celebrate their family history is something she feels strongly about.

title: Skillet: Comatose 20 Years, Still Screaming Tour
description:
After nearly three decades, eleven albums, and thousands of shows worldwide, Skillet play louder, fight harder, and sound more rebellious than ever. As of 2024, the band have received two-time GRAMMY® Award nominations, picked up a Billboard Music Award, and landed three albums in the Top 5 of the Billboard 200. Selling over 22 million units worldwide, they have notched multiplatinum, platinum, or gold RIAA certifications for a total of 12 singles and four full-length albums. Not to mention, they have regularly attracted 10 million monthly listeners on Spotify, boasting “one of the most-streamed rock songs of all-time” with the 5x-platinum “Monster.” Their presence has impressively surged throughout popular culture with syncs by WWE, Marvel, ESPN, and NFL in addition to coverage from USA Today, The New York Times, and more. As a live force of nature, they have touched down on four continents and in 26 countries, packing arenas everywhere from the Middle East to Russia. Not to mention, Skillet expanded their world with the graphic novel series EDEN. The first installment stood out as Z2 Comics’ best-selling book of all-time. Now, the global hard rock quartet—John Cooper [lead vocals, bass], Korey Cooper [guitar, keys], Jen Ledger [drums, vocals], and Seth Morrison [lead guitar]—deliver an insurgent, infectious, and inimitable body of work with their twelfth full-length offering and first-ever independent album, Revolution, led by the single “Unpopular.”

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW

title: Jersey Central Farewell Summer Shore Hike
description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More!
Join us for this point to point hike in the north NJ shore region.
The theme of this one is of course the end of Summer, but also the historic Central Railroad of New Jersey.
The CNJ served a lot of shore points, and it's always fun to visit them on the hikes. So, for this one, we will focus on some of these rights of ways, including ones on the beach.
After meeting at the end point. Lot C at Sandy Hook, we will shuttle with as few vehicles as possible to a point south of Red Bank where there was a junction with the New York and Long Branch line.
The CNJ had a line to the east from here, which served Port Monmouth and continued east to a junction with the Seashore Branch.
We will trace this as closely as possible. Some bits of it are now trail, but they are very short. Some bits are now parking lots, gas lines, or roads. The route will take us through the raceway area, and then out toward the shore line.
We'll continue north following the rail grade as closely as possible, and eventually it turns into a walkway along the sea wall.
We'll continue on that walkway to the north to Sandy Hook, and probably at some point head to the water for a couple of breaks before the end.
There will be places for food and drinks along the way.
If needed, contact me at 908 343 8374

title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day
description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**TRAIL WORK (which was canceled Sept. 13th due to steady rain) will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays)
description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

title: UUCM Religious Education Registration
location: UU Congregation at Montclair, 67 Church Street, Montclair, NJ, United States
description:
Registration is now open for the Unitarian Universalist Congregation at Montclair’s 2026-2027 Religious Education (RE) program for children and youth. We are a liberal religious community seeking transformation in our hearts, our homes, our community, and our world. 
Religious Education (RE) Program Goals: The RE program aims to provide broad and connected Unitarian Universalist lifespan religious education for the community inside and outside our walls to ensure a vibrant, thriving congregation. 
The purpose of the Religious Education Program is to guide our children, youth, and adults in the ethical exploration of Unitarian Universalist Values. We help to nurture the curiosity of soul expansion and growth through fun and engaging structured learning and spiritual experiences that emphasize: 
Nurturing the individual spirit within our loving community.
Understanding that we are part of the Unitarian Universalist heritage, past, present, and future.
Cultivating curiosity about, appreciation for, and engagement with all faith traditions.
Developing a lifelong practice of service.
Encouraging mindfulness and a sense of wonder. 
PROGRAM INFO:
Unitarian Universalists are a covenantal, like-valued people. The covenants we make are intentional conversations about the value-based actions we expect from each other, and they hold us accountable and in community by giving everyone a voice. The Living Tradition of Unitarian Universalism is informed by growth and change. UUCM affirms and promotes the UU Values that call us to do something about what we believe ethically and responsibly. These UU Values are: 
Justice
Equity
Transformation
Pluralism
Interdependence
Generosity
These UU Values are all held together with the common thread of LOVE. 
Our RE Program provides a liberating faith education that instills values that emancipate minds and grow spirits. Our dogma-free approach centers the margins, widens the circle, and enlivens the human impulse to justice and love. 
Classes on Offer for 2026-2027:
4th/5th Grade OWL Class (4-5 in the Spring)
8th/9th Grade OWL – 8th & 9th grades
Living Into Social Justice – Trimester 1 of 8th/9th OWL
Creative Edge – 3rd to 5th grades
Dungeons & Dragons – 4th through 12th grades The D&D CLASS SIZE LIMIT is 8 students.
Neighboring Faiths – 6th & 7th grades
Values Room – K through 3rd grades (4-year-old Pre-K are allowed w/parent assisting, 5-year-olds are independent)
Youth Group (U-YG) – 9th through 12th grades 
HIKE! Two Special COMMUNITY-BUILDING Hiking Events, one in the Fall and one in the Spring: 
RE Friends & Families HIKES – Outdoor Education engages participants in practical and active learning experiences, typically in natural settings, to benefit the person, community, and nature. 
Detailed DESCRIPTIONS of our 2026-2027 Classes & Activity Groups offerings: 
OWL- 8th & 9th grade OWL (Oct 26 to May 27), and 4th & 5th grade OWL will take place in the Spring of 2027 – Our Whole Lives (OWL)
OWL is a comprehensive, lifespan sexuality education curriculum for use in both secular settings and faith communities. It dismantles stereotypes and assumptions, builds self-acceptance and self-esteem, fosters healthy relationships, improves decision-making, and has the potential to save lives. 
LIVING INTO SOCIAL JUSTICE – (ONLY for Trimester 1 pre-8th/9th grade OWL – formerly called Heeding The Call).
A social justice curriculum exploring ethical imagination and moral courage by examining societal oppression while encouraging an understanding of values that counteract the marginalization of others. Workshops on empathy, courage, abundance, joy, and other values ask participants to recognize how these standards can be tools for Justice. Additionally, the program includes concrete tools, such as suggestions on how to be a good ally and tips on the language of conflict resolution. 
CREATIVE EDGE – Best 3rd through 5th Grades. Multifaceted creative exploration of foundational UU values.
Students will learn how to frame our UU Values and concepts like dignity, justice, and compassion and to capture and convey powerful messages through creative projects using various media – Poetry, Spoken Word, Music, Painting, drawing, photography, fabric arts, etc. Creative Edge also engages with the wider UUCM congregation by inviting our creative congregants to share their special creative talents with the kids. Our multi-age learning environment encourages multi-age peer support and mentoring. 
THE VALUES ROOM – Best for Kindergarten through 3RD Grades and New to the U kids. Multifaceted creative exploration of foundational UU values.
Students will learn how to frame concepts like dignity, justice, and compassion and to capture and convey powerful messages through creative projects using various media. Our multi-age learning environment encourages multi-age peer support and mentoring. 
DUNGEONS & DRAGONS – For 4th through 12th grades. Explores CORE UU VALUES and TRADITIONS through D&D fantasy role-playing adventures.
A creative role-playing game where students create characters that offer kids who are already grappling with complicated questions about their lives ways to safely explore different aspects of themselves and society. Drop-Ins are limited (available only with advanced notice/Teacher permission). 
NEIGHBORING FAITHS (6th & 7th Grades)
In the Neighboring Faith class, young people become better citizens by learning about other faith communities, through field trips to those faith communities. We focus on three important dimensions of religion; the emotional, the material, and the social. We learn about these dimensions of religion by experiencing the worship services of other faith communities. 
UU YOUTH GROUP (U-YG)
Service opportunities and Youth bonding experiences through regular meetings and interactions within the ministry areas of UUCM.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776”
description:
The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. 
Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013.
Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ.
The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. 
With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. 
Those auditioning should prepare 16 to 32 bars of a song and bring sheet music for the accompanist. A bluetooth speaker will be available if needed. Actors will also be asked to read selections from the script. Please bring a résumé and photo. 
For information on cast and characters, please visit https://www.theaterleagueofclifton.com/ or email theaterleagueofclifton@gmail.com or call (973)-928-7668 
Founded in 2005, the Theater League of Clifton is a nonprofit community organization dedicated to fostering an appreciation of the arts through theatrical performances while providing quality entertainment for all ages. The Theater League of Clifton welcomes volunteers in all aspects of performance and production. 
1776
Music and Lyrics by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Book by PETER STONE
Based on a concept by SHERMAN EDWARDS
Original Production Directed by PETER HUNT
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by STUART OSTROW
1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI.

As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.”  This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.

"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . .  A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . .  with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

Kaliane Bradley is a British-Cambodian writer and editor based in London. Her short fiction has appeared in Somesuch Stories, The Willowherb Review, Electric Literature, Catapult, and Extra Teeth, among others. She was the winner of the 2022 Harper’s Bazaar Short Story Prize and the 2022 V.S. Pritchett Short Story Prize.

title: Pasta with a Twist: A Fresh Take on Italian Classics with Food Network Star Joe Sasto
description:
It’s time to ditch the same boring recipes and bring big, playful creativity back into your kitchen! Join us for an online conversation with Top Chef finalist and Food Network star Joe Sasto as we explore his hit national bestselling cookbook, Breaking the Rules: A Fresh Take on Italian Classics. 

Whether you are a novice cook looking to build your kitchen confidence or an experienced chef eager to expand your culinary repertoire, Joe’s approachable philosophy will change how you view everyday ingredients. We will dive deep into his vibrant world of handcrafted pasta, step-by-step rolling techniques, and unexpected flavor profiles. 

From foundational family favorites like his mom’s red sauce to daring, crave-worthy creations like Corn Cacio e Pepe, Marinated Tomato “Amatriciana,” and Pesto Pinwheel Pull-Apart Bread, this conversation is an open invitation to trust your culinary instincts and cook with absolute freedom.

Register today and learn how to make cooking fun again!

 

About the Author: 

Celebrity chef Joe Sasto found his love for cooking and appetite for Italian classics as a child at his mother's side. When the COVID-19 pandemic hit in March 2020, he pivoted his career by teaching virtual pasta-making classes.

With more than half a billion likes and countless viral social media videos, Sasto has become a recurring judge and chef personality across multiple shows on the Food Network. He's also competed and appeared on Food Network shows such as Guy Fieri's Tournament of Champions, Guy's Grocery Games, and Chopped, as well as Bravo's Top Chef and Top Chef All-stars.

In 2022, Sasto made the Food Network's first-ever "Hot List." Aside from his career as a chef, Sasto has developed a high-end customizable pasta and pizza tool line, and he is the creator of Tantos, the first puffed pasta chip, and a gourmet frozen ravioli brand, Ripi. His first cookbook, Breaking the Rules – a fresh take on Italian classics, was published in October 2025. He lives in Chicago and enjoys spending time with his pup, Tito, and his wife, Kait.

title: The American Experiment ;Migration, Identity, and the American Nation
description:
Join President Koppell for his first lecture in the American Experiment series, where he will discuss migration, identity, and the American nation.
Migration has been central to the American experience from the nation’s earliest history to the present. It has shaped the country’s population, economy, politics, culture, and understanding of national identity, while also generating recurring debates over citizenship, belonging, borders, assimilation, and exclusion. This lecture examines how migration, including internal and forced migration, has influenced the development of the United States and how Americans have defined who belongs within the national community. It considers the tensions between the country’s long-standing identity as a nation of immigrants and its equally significant history of restriction, exclusion, and contested membership. The discussion will explore how race, ethnicity, religion, class, and demographic change have shaped immigration policy and public attitudes, while placing contemporary debates over borders, citizenship, birthright citizenship, integration, and national identity within a broader historical and constitutional context. At its center is an enduring question for American democracy: How should a nation shaped by migration define membership, belonging, and shared identity in a period of rapid global and demographic change?

title: Tuesday Night Open Studio Figure Drawing
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Every Tuesday, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies – charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. 
Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space.

title: Union Cong Discusses: The Sum of Us (Guild Room)
description:
The Racial Justice Ministry Team is sponsoring a 2-session book discussion of The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs Everyone and How We Can Prosper Together by Heather McGhee, in advance of the townwide Open Book/Open Mind program: Heather McGhee in conversation with Michelle Alexander (free with registration) on October 13.  
The book traces the history of how some communities, faced with integration, chose instead to defund, eliminate, and ultimately privatize public goods such as public swimming pools. But there is a better, more hope-filled way: to grow the pie to benefit everyone and collect the Solidarity Dividend.   
Join Union members and friends for pizza and discussion of key book topics (summary sheets available for download in advance) and personal reflection on September 29 and October 6 from 7 pm – 8:30 pm in the Main Building. Discussion topics will be different each week, so please plan to attend one or both sessions! Please RSVP here so we can be sure to have enough pizza. This is an intergenerational event for Middle Schoolers through Adult.  
Many of you already have a copy of the book. If you don’t yet have a copy, feel free to pick one up (it’s available in both adult and young adult versions) from your local library or favorite book vendor or reach out to Ina Isobe (ina.isobe@gmail.com) for a church library copy.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

What does it take to create lasting social change - and what can the history of LGBTQ+ activism teach us about today's battles over education, identity, and civil rights?
Join journalist and cultural commentator Tracy E. Gilchrist, host of Holding Space with Tracy E. Gilchrist and former editor-in-chief of The Advocate for a lively conversation with Professor Lisa M. Stulberg, NYU sociologist of education and author of the new book How to Win a Culture War: LGBTQ+ Social Change Through Pop Culture.
Drawing on Stulberg's research into LGBTQ+ social movements, education, and political change-and Gilchrist's years covering the intersections of LGBTQ+ equality, politics, and popular culture-the conversation will explore how movements change public attitudes, institutions, and policy; why cultural conflicts become so powerful; and what history can teach us about navigating the culture wars of the present.
An engaging conversation about activism, education, media, politics, and the possibilities for social change. This program will include audience participation and a speed round of LGBTQ+ trivia!

title: Breaking the Silence: Understanding Depression, Suicide, and the Power of Connection
description:
Presentation by Dr. Jason Dean and Dr. Rae Dumont

Depression is often misunderstood, accompanied with shame, secrecy or blame. So is suicide. The impact a loss by suicide has on friends and family is enormous. Without open conversations, people often feel alone as they carry the memory and question themselves about what they might have done to help. 

This presentation, in the context of a rising incidence of depression, anxiety and suicide, aims to offer understanding and compassion for people who struggle with mental illness. It  offers insights and comfort to those who have loved a person with depression, and tried to help. 

 

There will be ample time for discussion and for questions.

 

Rae Dumont, MD, LMFT, is both a pediatrician and a family therapist. While she practiced and taught at Harvard Medical School, she focused on the impact of one person's illness through the entire family, and on the interconnection between mental and physical health. 

In her family therapy practice, she helped people navigate difficulties by collaborating, rather than becoming divided. 

She is also a mother, a widow, and a friend to many. She now turns her experiences into words that speak of resilience, and the flawed road toward becoming good enough. In her fiction, she finds a personal, intimate voice, which connects emotionally with her readers’ humanity.

In the Shadow of Silence, (2-17-2026) is a novel about love, family life, and depression. She hopes for it to bring insight and comfort to her readers. 

 

Jason Dean, MD is a child and adult psychiatrist and founder of The Center for Developmental Psychiatry, a group practice in Teaneck, NJ. He is also a Clinical Instructor at Yale School of Medicine.

In his clinical work, he has worked to integrate a biological, medical view of psychiatry with a psychological perspective. Dr. Dean hopes to augment the discussion with insight gained from his clinical experience and training, as well as his work with families of individuals struggling with depression.

title: The Italian Job: Jason Horowitz in conversation with Mark Rotella
location: School of Communication and Media, Presentation Hall
description:
Please complete this RSVP form to confirm your registration! School of Communication and Media, Presentation Hall Wednesday, Oct. 7 at 6:00pm
The Coccia Institute at Montclair State University welcomes New York Times Rome bureau correspondent Jason Horowitz to discuss The Italian Job with Coccia director Mark Rotella.
 
From Venetian canals to Vatican conclaves, New York Times correspondent Jason Horowitz takes you on a tour of the real Italy.
 
Italy’s deep history, stunning landscapes and glorious food have uniquely captured our imagination. In The Italian Job, Jason Horowitz, a longtime Rome bureau chief for The New York Times, tells the story of how he too fell under that Tuscan-sun enchantment, before ultimately discovering a more fascinating Italy, a country conducting experiments in populist politics, confronting global challenges like immigration, climate change and an aging population.
 
Horowitz introduces us to an extraordinary range of characters. He flies with popes and drinks Spritzes with prime ministers, talks beauty with top fashion designers in Milan, ponders the big questions with cardinals in Rome, and gets his feet wet in the Venice lagoon with engineers trying to save the sinking city. Throughout, Italy’s streets, layered with history, and its cafés, vibrating with conversation, are full of lessons. So is his life at home, where his Italian wife and their two children offer an even more intimate, concentrated and rollicking view of Italian life. As years pass and the world turns upside down, Italy, more than a vacation destination or land of the past, reveals itself as a vivid lens through which to understand our present and future.

location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Join us for a trip up the Hackensack River from the southern Meadowlands to heart of the city of Hackensack. Taking the route once traveled by the coastal schooners and steamers that carried cargo to and from Bergen County, we will pass the ruins of their former docks and landings and discuss the region’s all-but-forgotten maritime history. title: CANCELLED - Everything Book Club, "The Ministry of Time" by Kaliene Bradley
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
An instant New York Times bestseller. In the near future, a new government ministry is exploring time travel. Our heroine gets a highly paid job assisting and monitoring the time travel expat known as “1847” or Commander Graham Gore. As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.”  This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.

"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . .  A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . .  with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

Kaliane Bradley is a British-Cambodian writer and editor based in London. Her short fiction has appeared in Somesuch Stories, The Willowherb Review, Electric Literature, Catapult, and Extra Teeth, among others. She was the winner of the 2022 Harper’s Bazaar Short Story Prize and the 2022 V.S. Pritchett Short Story Prize.

title: Art in Flight: Reinventing Postmodernism with Smithsonian Curator Carolyn Russo
description:
Join us for a captivating online conversation with acclaimed author and Smithsonian curator Carolyn Russo as we dive into her fascinating book, The Ascent of Rauschenberg. Explore the towering legacy, unexpected inspirations, and creative heights of one of America's most influential artistic icons.

Most famous for his groundbreaking "Combines"—painting and sculpture hybrids that often incorporated everyday objects—American artist Robert Rauschenberg (1925-2008) created within a range of mediums, including collage, performance, photography, and printmaking. But a connective tissue through it all was his fascination with flight. The Ascent of Rauschenberg explores the flight motif across his work, spanning birds, insects, aviation, spaceflight, sensory experiences, and metaphors for his own life.

More than 150 images reveal the vibrant scope of his work, from lithographs inspired by the Apollo 11 launch that NASA invited him to witness and document, to a Combine featuring a taxidermied eagle that evokes Roman mythology. Nine accompanying essays reflect on his many flight themes and subtleties that might otherwise be overlooked. The book also includes archival photographs and personal papers from the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation.

Register now for the chance to view art history through the unique prism of flight. 

About the Author:

Carolyn Russo is curator of the art collection at the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum. She has lectured internationally on the subject of art and flight and is the author of several publications including The Ascent of Rauschenberg: Reinventing the Art of Flight, Art of the Airport Tower, In Plane View: Abstractions of Flight, and Women and Flight: Portraits of Contemporary Women Pilots.

Complete the certification by following the step-by-step instructions provided in this link.

title: Faculty Concert: Chris Opperman, Composition
description:
Faculty Concert: Chris Opperman, Composition
Dr. Chris Opperman wields a special array of expertise. He is a composer of wildly original music, a top orchestrator and arranger, a dedicated and visionary educator, and a trusted advisor for an incredible cross-section of the music industry.
Since starting his Purple Cow Records label in 1998, Dr. Opperman has released six prior albums including 2001’s Klavierstücke, his first solo piano album, and 2010’s The Lionheart, an orchestral rock album. He has also released three EP’s including 2022’s Four Improvisations which feature studio-manipulated piano works, and two singles including “And If You Know” featuring Robert Martin.
With Arnie & Eric Roth of AWR Music, Dr. Opperman has worked on several national and international orchestral and chamber music tours including Distant Worlds: music from FINAL FANTASY, A New World: intimate music from FINAL FANTASY, the FINAL FANTASY VII Remake Orchestra World Tour, The Beach Boys Holiday Vibrations Orchestra Tour, several Mannheim Steamroller Christmas tours, and Undertale LIVE. Dr. Opperman’s arrangements with AWR and others have been performed by renowned and accomplished orchestras at premiere venues which include Carnegie Hall, the Royal Albert Hall, the Tokyo International Forum, and more.
Along with much other music, Opperman played piano on two of Steve Vai’s Grammy-nominated compositions, “Lotus Feet” from Real Illusions: Reflections and “The Attitude Song” from Sound Theories, Vols. I and II, both with the Metropole Orkest. He’s also performed with virtuoso multi-instrumentalist Mike Keneally, Indian classical music masters L. Shankar (a.k.a. Shenkar) and Zakir Hussein, former Duran Duran/Missing Persons guitarist Warren Cuccurullo, and many others.
Dr. Opperman holds a Ph. D. In Music Composition and has taught undergraduate and graduate level courses on music theory and composition, popular and classical music history, music technology, and the music industry.
Learn more about Chris Opperman

title: Two Eyes Screening Event
location: Montclair Main - Auditorium, Montclair Public Library
description:
Newark LGBTQ Center, Out Montclair and The Montclair Public Library invite you to an exclusive screening of Two Eyes, featuring Academy Award nominee Lily Gladstone.

In 19th century Montana, a painter's worldview is challenged by his Native American guide while exploring a new landscape. In 1970s California, a teenager’s life is shaken up by the arrival of an enigmatic transfer student. In present-day Wyoming, a trans youth attempts to work through his complex emotions with a nonbinary therapist. Two Eyes weaves together three distinct tales of queer identity into a single narrative exploring the power of human connection.

IN-PERSON SCREENING: Friday, October 9th at 7:00 p.m. EDT at the Montclair Library followed by a 45-minute live Zoom conversation with filmmaker Travis Fine. There is a suggested cash-only donation of $20.

Content Warning(s): Racially or Sexually Motivated Violence. This film does not have a formal rating, but overall themes are mature.

North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

title: "Tales from Ovid" by Ted Hughes: Read-Aloud and Discussion of an Often Banned Poet NEW
location: Montclair Main - Tower Room, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

The Roman poet Ovid has been upsetting censors for more than two thousand years. The emperor Augustus exiled Ovid from Rome shortly after the publication of his Metamorphoses. All Ovid's works were burned by Savonarola in the infamous "bonfire of the vanities" in 1497. And when Shakespeare's rival Christopher Marlowe translated Ovid a century later, the translation was set on fire again in the "Bishop's Ban." Then the U.S. Customs censored some of Ovid's work again in 1930.

To celebrate Banned Books Week, we'll be reading aloud and discussing "Tales from Ovid: 24 Passages from the Metamorphoses," an award-winning retelling by the longtime British poet laureate Ted Hughes. Come to class and hear for yourself what all fuss is about!

North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More
Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.

⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.

🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).

**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one court.

**🧯DISCLAIMER:** Courts are subject to availability and weather. If you make plans to attend please be prepared to cancel or adjust our location as needed. Furthermore, by attending you agree to be fully responsible for your own health and safety. Each person is responsible to take a break for rest and water at their own discretion.

South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group
**Sunday, October 11, 3 - 5:30pm**

Free expert-led hike in South Mountain Reservation. Hike about 2-3 hours covering 3-4 miles at a modest pace over rocky trails with one long climb from the Rahway River up South Mountain. Focus on ecology and hydrology, led by Dr. Kirk Barrett, President of the Rahway Watershed Association and expert on local watershed issues. Good balance required. Children welcome. No dogs.

	Clean and gently used hardcover and softcover books: adult and children, English and other languages, fiction and nonfiction.
	DVDs, Blu-rays, CDs, & audio book CDs in their original printed jackets or cases. No VHS or cassette tapes, 78’s, or self-recorded media

We CANNOT ACCEPT anything that is:


	Falling apart
	Moldy
	Heavily underlined

title: Kichwa Language Workshop Series
description:
LAIC (LATIN AMERICAN INDIGENOUS COLLABORATIVE) at CLaSE invites the Montclair State University community and the broader public to participate in our Kichwa Language & Culture Workshop Series, beginning Monday, September 14.
This 10-week workshop series offers participants the opportunity to learn Kichwa while exploring the language, culture, and traditions of Kichwa-speaking communities. Workshops are conducted in Spanish and Kichwa by our amazing and well known Kichwa community leaders - Atik Paguay and Fabian Muenala and are open to students, faculty, staff, families, and community members from outside the University. No previous knowledge of Kichwa is required.
Mondays, beginning September 145:30–7:30 p.m.Cole Hall, Room 14110-week series
We invite everyone interested in Indigenous languages and cultures to join us. Registration is required by contacting Dr. Calarota-Ninman at  calarotaa@montclair.edu

title: Finish Strong and Position Your Business for Growth
description:
Montclair Business Networking
Year-end has a way of sneaking up on business owners. You’re focused on finishing the year strong while budgets need attention, next year’s marketing plan is taking shape, staffing decisions are looming, and new growth goals are already on the table.
Before you start setting goals for 2027, there are some bigger questions worth asking:

* What drove your growth this year and where did you fall short?

* Does your team have the capacity and skills to support where you want to go?

* Are your marketing, financial, and operational plans working together toward the same goals?

Join us on October 13th and we’ll help you unpack it.
The panel discussion brings together experts in business growth, marketing, HR, and accounting to help you build a stronger foundation for the year ahead.
Topics include:

* 2026 Performance Review: What your financial results, marketing performance, and workforce health say about where your business stands.

* 2027 Growth Planning: Marketing, financial, and workforce decisions to make now as you set your goals for the new year.

* Execution Readiness: The people, processes, systems, and financial foundation you need in place to carry out your plan.

Who Should Attend?

* Business owners and entrepreneurs

* CEOs and senior leaders

* Sales and marketing leaders

* HR and people leaders

* Business development professionals

* Anyone responsible for helping their organization grow in 2027

Don’t wait until January to figure out what 2027 should look like. Use this session to take stock of where your business stands, identify what needs attention, and head into the new year ready to act.
Reserve your spot!

title: AMERICAN HIGHER EDUCATION: FOUNDATION OF DEMOCRACY, ENGINE OF INNOVATION
description:
American higher education evolved from an elite system training clergy into a vital pillar of our democracy and economic progress. While the nation's Founders recognized the essential link between education and self-governance, contemporary universities did not initially serve this broader public purpose.
The first dramatic shift came during the Civil War, when the Morrill Act of 1862 established land-grant universities with a public mission to train citizens in building the infrastructure and agricultural capacity of a developing nation. This democratic commitment expanded over the decades to include African Americans through the 1890 Morrill Act and to train educators via normal schools, like Montclair, at the turn of the century. Following World War II, the "Endless Frontier" report permanently linked university research with national security and industrial strength. This model, combined with the GI Bill's massive expansion of student access and the Bayh-Dole Act's incentives for commercializing intellectual property, established higher education as the primary engine of modern innovation.
Today, universities sit at the center of critical national policy, where federal investments simultaneously ensure democratic access through student aid and drive advanced economic initiatives. With many questioning the value of higher education, this lecture provides analysis of the current institutional landscape set in its historical context.

title: Crane's Mill:  The Story Behind the Name
location: West Caldwell - Community Meeting Room, West Caldwell Public Library
description:
Join local historian Bob Williams on Tuesday, October 13 at 6:30 p.m. at the West Caldwell Public Library for a fascinating look at the history of Crane’s Mill and its connection to West Caldwell.

The story has a personal connection for Williams. When he was just 15 years old, he purchased a collection of historic ledgers from Crane’s Sawmill in West Caldwell. By then, the mill had already been dismantled and moved to Allaire Village in South Jersey for reconstruction although it was never rebuilt. The mill’s foundation ruins remained in West Caldwell for years, becoming a favorite place for Williams to explore throughout his youth and into adulthood.

title: Open Book / Open Mind; Heather McGhee; "The Sum of Us." With Michelle Alexander.
location: Montclair - First Congregational Church of Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
What if we've been looking at opportunity in America all wrong? What if individual groups stopped trying to get a larger slice of the pie and worked together to create a bigger, better pie? 

Join the Montclair Public Library and Partners for Health Foundation for an inspiring conversation between Heather McGhee, an influential economic and public policy expert, and Michelle Alexander, a renowned civil rights lawyer and author. They'll be talking about "The Sum of Us: What Racism Costs Everyone and How We Can Prosper Together," McGhee's landmark New York Times bestseller from 2021 about how overcoming racism helps everyone, not just people of color, and how to move beyond the zero-sum vision of American opportunity.  

After the discussion, there will be a Q&A period, followed by signing with Watchung Booksellers. 

Thanks to the generosity of Partners for Health Foundation, free copies of “The Sum of Us” will be available to the first 50 guests to enter (who have not already received books in the Library’s community read). 

Join our community read, Montclair Reads "The Sum of Us," between June and October to get ready for this exceptional evening. Thanks to the generosity of Partners for Health, we'll be giving away free books to book clubs while supplies last. Click here for more details and to find out about other supporting programs. 

The event will take place at the First Congregational Church of Montclair, 40 S. Fullerton Avenue. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. The event is free but registration is required.

Open Book / Open Mind is sponsored by Montclair Public Library Foundation, Watchung Booksellers, Anonymous Dr. Alex and Doris Malaspina, David and Mary Lee Jones, and our individual Underwriters. title: Tuesday Open Studio Figure Drawing
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Every Tuesday, 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space | All skill levels welcome 
*Cover art by Ling Chen. 











Tuesday night at The Space is your invitation to drop in, find your creative flow, and practice your drawing skills. 
Each week a different model – usually nude, and sometimes clothed – serves as our muse as we pursue creative expression through observation and mark making. We challenge how we see and what we want to say, observing the nuances of the human form, its moods, character, and light — and do our best to capture something in the moment that tells a story. 
This has become a supportive community of seekers, artists, experimenters, and curious souls drawn together by the shared pursuit of capturing the living human form. Use the time to refine your skills, experiment with different media, and deepen your understanding of anatomy, gesture, and proportion. Challenge your process if you have one, or begin to develop one if you don’t. Learn to truly see. 
Each session features a variety of poses, from quick gesture sketches to longer, more detailed studies. Whether you’re looking to sharpen your technical abilities, loosen up your line work, or simply enjoy the meditative experience of drawing from life, this open studio is designed to support individual growth in a collaborative atmosphere. All skill levels are welcome – we’ve even had poets drop in and compose verses to the vibe in the room. 
Bring your preferred supplies – charcoal, graphite, ink, pastels, and paint are all welcome. 
Basic drawing materials are available if you don’t have any, and the shop has drawing pads and supplies for sale. No formal instruction is provided, but peer feedback and self-guided exploration are always part of the mix. 
Good music. Good people. See you Tuesday. 7 – 9:30 pm at the Space. 
Tickets are set at a capacity of 12, but we accommodate up to 18 for those paying in cash. 











“The object isn’t to make art, its to be in that wonderful state which makes art inevitable.” – Robert Henri

title: All In: The Fight for Democracy Film Screening & Civic Engagement Experience
description:
Democracy doesn't protect itself—it depends on informed, engaged citizens.
Join Civic and Voter Engagement, in collaboration with the African American Caucus, for a powerful screening of All In: The Fight for Democracy, the critically acclaimed documentary that examines the history and present-day reality of voter suppression in the United States. Featuring voting rights advocate Stacey Abrams, the film explores the historical barriers, systemic inequities, and ongoing challenges that continue to shape access to the ballot box and influence civic participation.
More than a documentary, this screening is an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the democratic process, reflect on the importance of protecting voting rights, and engage in meaningful dialogue about one of the most fundamental rights in our democracy.
Following the screening, participants are invited to stay for a facilitated discussion exploring the themes of the film, the significance of voting rights in today's political landscape, and the role each of us can play in strengthening our democracy through civic engagement. Whether you're new to these conversations or actively engaged in public life, this discussion offers a welcoming space to learn from one another, share perspectives, and consider how informed civic participation can create positive change.
Join us for:

A screening of the award-winning documentary All In: The Fight for Democracy
A facilitated discussion on the film's relevance to today's political climate
Meaningful conversation with fellow students, faculty, and staff
Free food and refreshments
Civic-themed giveaways
Resources to help you stay informed and engaged

This event is open to all students, faculty, and staff. Come for the film, stay for the conversation, and leave with a deeper understanding of the importance of civic participation and the power of every voice.
Good film. Great conversation. Free food. Giveaways. One important conversation about the future of our democracy.

title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes)
description:
The Mindful Stream
In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.

There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.

Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.

Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.

The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.

title: New Jersey's 44th Annual Law School Day
description:
Are you thinking about applying to law school? Join us for our 44th Annual NJ Law School Day at Montclair State University! All NJ college students and alumni who are interested in applying to law school are welcome to attend!
At NJ Law School Day, you can speak with law school representatives from NJ, NY, and across the U.S. about what their programs have to offer and how you can prepare to be a strong law school candidate.  Whether you are new to the idea of applying to law school or preparing to apply this fall, this event is a great opportunity to learn and connect.

 
What to Expect from Law School Day:
1pm - 2pm - Law School Panel Discussion
- For this session, you will hear from a panel of law school representatives about what they look for when reviewing law school applications and how to become a strong law school candidate.
 
2 - 4pm - The Law School Fair
- This is your chance to meet face-to- face with law school representatives from NJ, NY, PA, MA and across the U.S., and ask questions about applying to law school!
- The list of law schools attending is growing! Current law schools attending include: American, Fordham, Villanova, Ohio State, Seton Hall, Rutgers, Drexel, Penn State, Pace, Syracuse, Cardozo, Utah, Maryland, West Virginia, Richmond, Pittsburgh, and many, many more.  
- You can see the full list of law schools attending once you RSVP on Handshake on or after September 1, 2026
 
3:30 - 4:30 PM - Speed Mentoring: Pathways to Public Service
- After learning what it takes to get into law school, stick around to connect directly with professionals who are doing the work.  
- Through fast-paced, small-group rotating conversations, you’ll discover real-world career paths, and get honest insights into public interest and public service work. Come listen, ask questions, grab a snack, and make connections that can kickstart your legal, public interest, or public service career.
 
How to Be Prepared for Law School Day:

Be ready to share information about you, your interests, and your goals!
Write down the questions you have about law schools and the process of applying to law school
Bring something to take notes
Dress to impress!  Business attire is recommended
Registration for Law School Day will open on September 1, 2026 on Handshake
Questions? Need law school advice? Email Chrysten Colacicco, Pre-Law Program Coordinator at MSU, at colaciccoc@montclair.edu

description:

Julia Strayer, CPWA®, CIMA®, CRPC® Senior Vice President, Wealth Management Advisor.  Prior to joining Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2000, Julia was a vice president and private banker for BankBoston’s Private Bank for 7 years, responsible for asset management and trust services. Julia has appeared on the CNBC show “Power Lunch,” CBS “This Morning,” WGCH’s “Women in Business,” in addition to featured articles in USA Today.

Liz Maccarone, CRPC® Senior Financial Advisor.  Liz joined Merrill Lynch Wealth Management in 2012. Liz works closely with high-net-worth individuals and their families to create personalized and comprehensive strategies that support their goals, including investment management, retirement planning, liability management, and multigenerational planning. Liz values the importance of establishing and cultivating relationships with families including the next generation. Liz graduated from Fairfield University with a dual bachelor’s degree in Finance and Marketing. She began her career working at a boutique investment firm as a Business Development Associate, specializing in commodities and futures trading.

title: The Winding History of School Sports: A Unique American Invention NEW
description:
This is a paid Adult School class taking place at the Yogi Berra Museum. Click here to register.

Why do American schools build stadiums, award athletic scholarships, pay coaches extravagant salaries even as academic programs get cut, and turn teenagers into campus heroes - while most of the world keeps sports completely separate from education? This lively talk explores the surprising history behind the uniquely American idea of the "student-athlete". By comparing the US system with the European model of independent sports clubs, we'll uncover how this unusual partnership began, why it became so powerful, and what it means for education - and the futures - of young athletes today.

title: Wine Confidence 101
location: Montclair - Cornerstone Montclair, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Build your wine confidence in just four weeks. Whether you are new to wine or already a
connoisseur, this approachable course will give you the knowledge, tasting skills, and
vocabulary to enjoy wine more fully—and choose it more confidently.

Throughout this 4-week course, you will explore the world’s primary grape varieties and
discover the many styles of white, rosé, red, and sparkling wines. We will break down
the basics of viticulture and winemaking so you can understand how grapes, regions,
and production choices shape the flavors, aromas, body, and texture in every glass. You
will also learn what makes the major wine-producing countries distinctive and how to
recognize key differences among grape varieties and wine styles.

Each session includes guided tasting practice, from visual assessment through aroma,
flavor, structure, and finish, helping you evaluate wine and learn why you like or dislike
different wines. Durin the 4 weeks, we will taste 20–25 wines from around the world,
making this class both educational and delicious. By the end, you will feel more
comfortable ordering, buying, discussing, and enjoying wine in any setting.

THIS EVENT IS 21  Students will be required to show a government ID to the instructor
upon arriving at the first session.

title: Building Your Financial Roadmap: A Financial Wellness Series
location: Montclair Bellevue Ave Branch - First Floor, Montclair Bellevue Avenue Branch
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Take control of your financial future with this four-part financial wellness workshop series designed to help you build a stronger foundation for making informed money decisions. Each workshop focuses on a practical aspect of financial wellness, from understanding how money grows and creating a plan for where your money should go, to preparing your family and planning for retirement.

Whether you're just getting started, looking to strengthen your financial habits, or preparing for the future, you'll gain practical knowledge, useful tools, and actionable strategies you can apply to your own financial life.

Each week we'll answer one important question about your financial future:


	
	How does money grow?
	



	
	Where should my money go first?
	



	
	How do I prepare my family for the future?
	



	
	How do I prepare myself for retirement?
	


Whether you attend one workshop or the entire series, you'll leave with practical knowledge and actionable steps to help you make informed financial decisions.

These workshops are for educational purposes only and are intended to provide general financial education. They should not be considered individualized financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

title: Home Repair Essentials
location: Montclair - Montclair High School, Montclair Public Library
description:
This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.

Learn the fundamentals of home repair in this practical, hands-on workshop taught by Robert Haas, instructor of the popular Woodworking 101 and Advanced Woodworking classes. Held at Montclair High School, this course gives participants a behind-the-walls look at how common home features are built and maintained.

During the class, instructor Rob Haas will construct two demonstration walls that include doors and a window, showing how these elements are installed and how typical wall structures are assembled. Participants will also learn how traditional double-hung windows operate and how they can be repaired, including basic glass pane replacement.

The workshop will also introduce the basics of residential wiring, demonstrating how outlets and lighting are installed and connected. Throughout the session, Robert will answer questions and offer guidance on a wide range of home repair topics.

Whether you're a homeowner looking to handle basic repairs yourself or simply curious about how things in your home work, this class provides practical knowledge you can use right away.

title: The Space for Music - Jose Bevia Trio with special guest Sergio Albacete
location: the Space, 356 Bloomfield Ave, Montclair, New Jersey, 07042
description:
Wednesday, October 14 | doors open at 7:30, show starts at 8 pm | sliding scale tickets $25 – $30 
Co-hosted by Seed Artists 
The Space for Music with the Jose Bevia Trio and special guest Sergio Albacete, visiting from Spain. 
Jose Bevia on piano and keyboard, Ronen Itzik on drums, Peter Slavov on bass, and Sergio Albacete on saxophone. 
This program explores the intersections of Andalusian musical tradition, contemporary jazz and improvisation, tracing connections between Spain, the United States, and Cuba. Across the eight works, traditional melodies and rhythmic practices are reframed through contemporary harmony, metric exploration, and spontaneous improvisation. 
The concert opens with Mononas, Sergio Albacete’s reharmonization of a traditional melody from Villanueva de la Reina in Jaén, Andalusia. Characterized by its distinctive major-key sonority and an unchanging melodic structure, the piece demonstrates how a traditional folk idiom can acquire new harmonic dimensions while retaining its essential identity. 
The Smell of the Sunshine, by José Beviá, shifts the focus to the Finger Lakes region of New York. Inspired by the light, landscape, and tranquility of Cayuga Lake, the composition combines influences from Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Bob Mintzer with unexpected metric shifts and evolving thematic material. 
In Tangos de Cazorla, Albacete draws on Andalusian folk traditions preserved in the mountainous regions of Cazorla and Segura. Incorporating the rhythms of tientos and tangos with the Andalusian cadence, the arrangement later engages with the harmonic language of John Coltrane, creating a dialogue between Andalusian tradition and American jazz. 
Nico-Lico, by José Beviá, explores the relationship between composition and improvisation. Influenced by post-bop, Latin music, and contemporary compositional practices, the work allows the soloist to shape the tempo and rhythmic flow, making time itself an element of musical interaction. Written and improvised passages gradually merge into a unified formal process. 
Eunidenserías, by Sergio Albacete, offers a contemporary perspective on the bulerías. Traditional flamenco rhythmic and melodic gestures encounter the metric and rhythmic concepts of modern jazz, particularly those associated with musicians such as Ari Hoenig. 
Sedona Valley, by José Beviá, is inspired by the dramatic landscapes of Sedona and the Grand Canyon. The composition translates the immense scale, vivid colors, and geological beauty of the American Southwest into a musical reflection on place and memory. 
Nana del Caballo Grande, based on the music of Camarón de la Isla and arranged by Sergio Albacete, revisits one of the defining works of La Leyenda del Tiempo. The arrangement connects Camarón’s modern flamenco language with the historic form of the caña, linking ancient Andalusian song traditions with the transformative aesthetics of 20th-century flamenco. 
The program concludes with La Guarida, José Beviá’s tribute to Cuban music and to a deeply personal moment in Havana. Inspired by a piano lesson with a Cuban musician, the composition develops a montuno as a recurring subject, transforming it through successive variations, improvisation, and bitonal passages. The piece ultimately becomes both a musical exploration and a personal narrative, named for the Havana restaurant where Beviá proposed to his wife, Maggie. 
BYOB is welcome, some light refreshments will be offered. 
  
Sergio Albacete is a Spanish multi-instrumentalist, composer, arranger, and researcher with a
distinguished 30-year career. He holds advanced studies in classical saxophone and a Master’s
Degree in Jazz Performance from Musikene. He has performed and conducted Big Bands for 25
years and has been a tenured faculty member at the “Ramón Garay” Professional Conservatory
since 2004.
Albacete has collaborated and performed with internationally renowned musicians including
Barry Harris, Eric Alexander, Kurt Elling, Lee Konitz, Jerry Bergonzi, Perico Sambeat, Marco
Mezquida, Enrique Morente, and Claude Delangle. His career has taken him across Spain,
Portugal, Denmark, Germany, the United States, and the United Arab Emirates, and he has
participated in more than 30 album recordings.
His distinctions include the 2015 Culture Award from the City Council of Torredelcampo, Best
Album at the 2016 Jaén Music Awards, the 2018 Musical Excellence Award from Diario Jaén, the
2024 Jaén Public Employment Award, and the 2026 Grajo Award for Modern Music and Other
Styles.

title: Prompting for Data People: Getting Real Work Out of Copilot and Claude
description:
Cloud Data Driven
Most data professionals have tried an AI assistant, got a mediocre answer, and quietly went back to Stack Overflow. The difference between mediocre and magical is the prompt — and prompting for DATA work has its own rules: schemas matter, sample rows matter, constraints matter, and “show your reasoning” beats “give me code”.

In this hands-on session I share the prompting method I use daily with GitHub Copilot and Claude across T-SQL, DAX and Python: how to give context without pasting your whole database, how to make the AI ask YOU clarifying questions, how to iterate instead of restarting, and how to spot the confident nonsense. Live demos throughout, including at least one glorious AI failure and how to catch it. Works with any assistant your company allows.

Attendees will learn a practical, repeatable prompting method for data work with GitHub Copilot and Claude: giving schema and sample-row context without oversharing, making the AI ask clarifying questions, iterating instead of restarting, and reviewing AI-generated T-SQL/DAX/Python before trusting it. They leave with a reusable prompt template and a checklist for reviewing AI-generated code.
